name: thailand-stay-plan
description: Thailand visa finder and rules, from public sources. Six read-only tools: rank the legal routes to stay in Thailand for a person (30-day exemption, tourist visa, DTV digital nomad visa, Non-O retirement, Non-O marriage or Thai family, LTR, Thailand Privilege, formerly Thailand Elite), explain one route's requirements, money test, fees, documents and where to apply, compare routes side by side over the years, check entry without a visa by passport, give immigration office addresses and hours, and list dated rule changes. Every fact carries its source and check date. Information, not legal advice.

author.name: Thailand Stay Plan (BRS Properties Co., Ltd.)

keywords: do I need a visa for Thailand

interface.longDescription:
Thailand visa finder for anyone who wants to visit, live, retire or work remotely in Thailand. Ask which visa fits you, what the Thailand retirement visa (Non-O, O-A) needs, how much the Thailand Elite visa (now Thailand Privilege) costs over 5 or 20 years, whether the DTV digital nomad visa or the LTR suits you, whether you need a visa for a holiday and how long you can stay, where your immigration office is and when it opens, or what changed in the rules.

Thailand Stay Plan answers with six read-only tools. The route finder ranks the seven legal routes to stay (the 30-day exemption with its extension, the tourist visa, the Destination Thailand Visa, the Non-O retirement route, the Non-O marriage or Thai family route, the Long-Term Resident visa from the Board of Investment, and Thailand Privilege) from your passport, age, money, planned stay, remote work and Thai family, with the same rules as the Visa Map on thailandstayplan.com. The other tools explain one route in detail (who can apply, money test, fees, documents, where to apply, processing time, insurance, work, family, extension), compare two to four routes side by side with the government cost over the years you choose, check entry without a visa for a passport after the 15 September 2026 change to 30 days, give the address, hours and counters of the main immigration offices, and list dated rule changes.

Every fact comes from a public source, mostly the Royal Gazette, the Immigration Bureau, the Ministry of Foreign Affairs and Thai embassies, the Board of Investment and Thailand Privilege Card Co., Ltd., and carries its source and check date. Thai rules changed in August and September 2026, so the app answers from these sources rather than from older general knowledge. When a fact you need is missing, it asks instead of guessing.

The app never asks for your name and keeps no answers or personal data. It explains published rules; it is not legal advice, and Thai missions and Immigration decide every case. It recommends no agent, insurer or product and takes no orders.
capabilities: Ranks the seven legal routes to stay in Thailand from passport, age, money, stay, remote work and Thai family
Explains one route: retirement visa (Non-O, O-A), DTV, LTR, Thailand Elite (Privilege), marriage, work, study
Compares two to four routes side by side, with the government cost over 5, 10 or 20 years
Checks entry without a visa and visa on arrival for any passport after the 15 September 2026 change
Bangkok, Pattaya, Chiang Mai, Phuket and Hua Hin immigration offices: address, hours, counters
Lists dated rule changes; every fact carries its public source and check date
defaultPrompt: I'm 62, American, with about 900,000 baht saved and a 40,000 baht monthly pension. How can I stay in Thailand for good?
Thailand Elite visa vs LTR visa over 10 years: which costs less and what do I get?
Do I need a visa for Thailand with a UK passport, and how long can I stay?

positive.description: Retiree over 50 with the deposit route. The user gives nationality, age, savings and pension in Thai baht and wants to stay for good. The app ranks the Non-O retirement route first, the DTV and Thailand Privilege as check one point, and names the LTR, marriage route, 30-day exemption and tourist visa as not fitting, each with its blocker.
positive.prompt: I'm 62, American, with about 900,000 baht saved and a 40,000 baht monthly pension. How can I stay in Thailand for good?
positive.expected_behavior: which_thai_visa is called with nationality American, age 62, stay years, savings_thb 900000 and monthly_income_thb 40000. The answer puts the Non-O retirement (extension route) first as fits, with 5-year cost 9,500 THB (5 x 1,900 THB), time 2+ months, no health insurance mandate, the 800,000 THB deposit seasoned 2 months before the first extension and 3 before later ones, the 400,000 THB floor and the note that agents charge 12,900-65,000 THB a year while filing yourself costs 1,900 THB. DTV and Thailand Privilege follow as check one point. LTR, Non-O marriage, 30-day exemption and tourist visa are listed as does not fit with a blocker each. Sources (Immigration Bureau Order 12/2568; ThaiLawOnline; Thailand Starter Kit), the check date 26 Oct 2026 and the sentence that this is not legal advice appear. The answer ends with a link to thailandstayplan.com. ChatGPT asks for no name and recommends no agent.

positive.description: Single-route question on the Thailand Elite visa (Thailand Privilege). The details tool returns the summary, the tier figures and the registered facts with sources.
positive.prompt: How much is the Thailand Elite visa and what tiers are there?
positive.expected_behavior: thai_visa_details is called with route "Thailand Elite visa" (topic overview or fees). The answer names Thailand Privilege as the current name, lists the membership tiers with their terms and fees as the tool returns them, keeps the sources and check date, says it is not legal advice and ends with the link to thailandstayplan.com. No agent is recommended.

positive.description: Comparison. The compare tool returns both routes side by side with the government cost over 10 years.
positive.prompt: Compare the LTR visa and the Thai retirement visa for a 60-year-old over 10 years.
positive.expected_behavior: compare_thai_visas is called with routes ["LTR visa", "retirement visa"], years 10 and age 60. The answer shows for each route the length, money test, work rights, family, insurance, reporting, where to apply and the cost over 10 years with its basis, notes that agent fees, insurance and living costs are not included, and ends with the link line.

positive.description: Entry check. A UK passport holder asks whether a visa is needed for a 45-day trip; the tool returns 30 days visa-free and the extension rule.
positive.prompt: Do I need a visa for Thailand? I'm British and want to stay 45 days.
positive.expected_behavior: thai_entry_check is called with nationality "British" and days 45. The answer says UK passport holders may stay up to 30 days without a visa for tourism since 15 Sep 2026, that 45 days is longer, that one 30-day extension at Immigration costs 1,900 THB, and mentions the TDAC arrival card, with sources and the link line.

positive.description: Immigration office. The office tool returns the Jomtien office fields and facts.
positive.prompt: Where is the immigration office in Pattaya and when is it open?
positive.expected_behavior: thai_immigration_office is called with place "Pattaya". The answer gives the Jomtien (Chonburi) office address, hours as the tool states them, services and what to bring, with sources, a note that hours change on holidays, and the link line.

negative.description: Not Thailand. The app covers Thailand only, so a question about another country's visa should not call the tool, or if called with no Thailand context ChatGPT should answer on its own without Thailand Stay Plan content.
negative.prompt: Which visa do I need to spend six months in Vietnam?

negative.description: Approval guarantee. The app explains published rules with sources and says that Thai missions and Immigration decide every case. Expected: no promise that any visa will be approved, at most the ranked routes with the disclaimer.
negative.prompt: Can you guarantee that my DTV application will be approved if I use your app?

negative.description: Unrelated travel task. Booking flights or hotels has nothing to do with the stay routes, so which_thai_visa should not be called and no Thailand Stay Plan content added.
negative.prompt: Find me a cheap flight from London to Bangkok next Friday.

review.commerce_description: The app sells nothing and processes no payments inside ChatGPT. Every figure it returns is a government fee, a bank threshold or the published membership fee of Thailand Privilege Card Co., Ltd., quoted with its public source as information; the app offers nothing for sale, takes no orders and links only to information pages on thailandstayplan.com. The website introduces licensed partners on some pages and discloses the commission there; the app itself names no agent and no insurer.

publication.release_notes: 1.1.0: Five new read-only tools next to which_thai_visa: thai_visa_details (one route's requirements, money test, fees, documents, where to apply, time, insurance, work, family, extension), compare_thai_visas (two to four routes side by side with the government cost over the chosen years), thai_entry_check (entry without a visa by passport after the 15 Sep 2026 change), thai_immigration_office (address, hours and counters of five main offices) and thai_visa_rule_changes (dated changes). which_thai_visa now also names the education visa, work permit and permanent residence when they matter. Every fact carries its public source and check date. Still no account, no name, no answers kept.
